findings.claim: Hashing the whole payload gives a stable idempotency key across a retry
Retrying an identical transfer without a key is safe by default
Equivalent amount strings yield the same semantic key
The premise an agent decided on still holds when its tx is included
The condition gate documents that it is not atomic with the action
A workflow whose action node never runs does not report success

report.summary: KeeperHub's execution guarantees mostly hold, with some caveats. Idempotency keys are not stable across retries unless only the semantic surface is hashed. Retrying an identical transfer without a key can lead to duplicate executions. Equivalent amount strings do not yield the same semantic key. Premise staleness can cause transactions to execute with an expired premise. The condition gate is not atomic with the action. A workflow with a skipped action node can still report success. However, concurrent distinct transfers are handled correctly, and reverting calls are reported as failed. Cross-chain key scope and overdraft transfers are also handled as expected.

probes.name: prose_drift
probes.claim: Hashing the whole payload gives a stable idempotency key across a retry
probes.detail: Same transaction, two executions. The payloads differ only in a free-text `reason` field the model rewrote: observed verbatim from llama-3.3-70b and gpt-oss-120b at temperature 0.

probes.name: semantic_key_fix
probes.claim: Hashing only the semantic surface survives prose drift
probes.detail: Both retries collapsed to one execution.

probes.name: omitted_key
probes.claim: Retrying an identical transfer without a key is safe by default
probes.detail: Two identical transfers, two executions. Duplicate protection is opt-in: an agent that never sets idempotency_key has none, and nothing warns it.

probes.name: concurrent_same_key
probes.claim: Simultaneous retries with one key produce exactly one execution
probes.detail: 4 concurrent calls -> 1 execution, 3 rejected 409 'already being processed'. The dedupe is atomic under concurrency: the race is serialised server-side rather than racing through.

probes.name: amount_formatting
probes.claim: Equivalent amount strings yield the same semantic key
probes.detail: '0.001' and '0.0010' are the same transfer but hash differently, so even the semantic key double-spends unless amounts are normalized before hashing. A model re-emitting a number in another format is enough.

probes.name: cross_chain_key_scope
probes.claim: Reusing a key with a different payload is caught, not silently applied
probes.detail: 409 'Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request payload'. The key is bound to the payload, so a cross-chain reuse is rejected outright rather than silently suppressing a legitimate transfer. This is the Stripe semantic done correctly.

probes.name: premise_staleness
probes.claim: The premise an agent decided on still holds when its tx is included
probes.detail: Decided at block 11395486 on the premise 'block <= 11395486'. Included at block 11395487, 1 block(s) later (12.6s). The premise was FALSE at inclusion and the transaction executed anyway. Simulation verifies feasibility, never justification, so this is invisible: the transaction succeeds and reports success.

probes.name: conditional_staleness
probes.claim: The condition gate documents that it is not atomic with the action
probes.detail: Condition 'block <= 11395487' evaluated true at block 11395487; the action was included at block 11395488, 1 block(s) later, where it is false. KeeperHub's own read-condition-act primitive carries the gap it exists to remove. Off-chain check-then-act cannot be atomic, so this is inherent rather than a defect: the issue is that nothing says so. The name and shape of the primitive imply the condition gates the action, and an agent handed it reasonably assumes enforcement at execution. Documented, this is a caveat; undocumented, it is a trap. A real fix needs an on-chain guard that re-checks in the same transaction.

probes.name: revert_reporting
probes.claim: A call that will revert is reported as failed, not completed
probes.detail: Reported status='failed', error='Contract call failed: execution reverted (no data present; likely require(false)'. The failure surfaces.

probes.name: overdraft_transfer
probes.claim: An unaffordable transfer is rejected cleanly, not left pending
probes.detail: status='failed', error='Insufficient ETH balance. Have: 0.05, Need: 1000000.0'. Failed cleanly; no nonce consumed.

probes.name: silent_noop_node
probes.claim: A workflow whose action node never runs does not report success
probes.detail: status='success' but executionTrace=['trigger-1']: the action node was skipped and the run still reported success, with error=None. The node was missing `actionType`; supplying it makes creation reject the workflow for a missing `abi`, so the *less* complete definition passes validation and silently does nothing, while the more complete one is caught. An agent sees a green run and an audit trail of success for an automation that never ran.

probes.name: parallel_distinct_transfers
probes.claim: Concurrent distinct transfers all land; none blocks the others
probes.detail: All 5 concurrent transfers completed. Nonces are allocated and submitted correctly under parallel load, so a busy agent does not head-of-line block itself: the failure mode that freezes naive senders.
